cast_dialogue.linea: Duty calls, heroes! 'Have to' is the obligation that life gives you — not the law, but your day.
I have to get up at six every day, and I have to walk the dog before work.
I have to study for my exams, but I don't have to wear a uniform at my school.
I have to answer a lot of emails. Do you have to work on Saturdays, Ben?
I don't have to work anymore, but I have to take my medicine and walk every day!

inicio.definicion_pragmatica: 'Have to' expresses external obligation (your job, your situation). It behaves like a normal verb: 'has to' for he/she/it, and questions/negatives with 'do/does'. Don't confuse it with 'must' (rules).
